AUTHOR: Francisco
TITLE: High-resolution, non-invasive animal tracking and reconstruction of local environment in aquatic ecosystems
REGION: STARESO, Corsica (Mediterranean) and Lake Tanganyika, Zambia
SPECIES: Conger conger, Mullus surmuletus, Diplodus vulgaris, Lamprologus callipterus
DATA: Own snorkel/SCUBA stereo and multi-camera videos: 'single', 'mixed', 'school' datasets plus 'accuracy' calibration-wand dataset
V_EV: Methods: 'The remaining datasets were collected via SCUBA (5-8 m) with either multi or stereo camera set-ups in Lake Tanganyika'
D_EV: no statement found (Methods only: 'models were able to accurately detect and segment the observed animals, which was visually confirmed with predictions on validation datasets')
R_EV: Methods: 'we trained Mask R-CNN models on small subsets of labeled video frames'; Training sets 'contained 171, 80 and 160 labeled images for the single, mixed and school datasets' (per-dataset models, no cross-domain test)
C_EV: Methods: 'filtering for linear motion over a short time window, reducing later quality control and manual track identification'; GUI for 'manual track corrections'
E_EV: Results: 'Trajectories were successfully obtained from large groups (school), small groups (mixed) and single individuals (single)'; accuracy validated only with calibration wand, not fish reference
ARCH: Mask R-CNN (Matterport) + Hungarian/nearest-neighbour tracking + COLMAP SfM triangulation, skeleton pose estimation
METR: RMSE/median of camera-to-camera reconstruction error (cm), reprojection error (px), calibration-wand tracking error (cm)
NOTE: Full text file is the bioRxiv preprint (Feb 2020, different title) of the Movement Ecology paper; coded PEER from metadata. INCL borderline: no quantitative detection metrics for fish (only 'visually confirmed'); quantitative results are SfM reconstruction/reprojection errors of fish tracks and wand tracking accuracy. C5 coded for stated manual track correction mechanism (could be argued 없음 -> C_ALL NR). E1 = behaviour/movement trajectories, not analysed further; no fish-level reference comparison. Turbidity/lighting statements only in Discussion (generic).
